ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $A$ is a point on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y = \frac{k}{x}$, and $AB$ is perpendicular to the $x$-axis at $B$. If the area of $\triangle AOB = 2$, what is the value of $k$?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, $A$ is a point on the graph of the inverse proportion function $y = \frac{k}{x}$, and $AB$ is perpendicular to the $x$-axis at $B$. If the area of $\triangle AOB = 2$, what is the value of $k$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is the origin, the x-axis is horizontal to the right, and the y-axis is vertical upward; the inverse proportional function curve is located near the first quadrant. Point A is on the curve, point B is on the x-axis, line segment AB is vertical downward and perpendicular to the x-axis, and line segment OA together with OB and AB forms triangle AOB. Reasoning: Let A=(a,b). From the figure it can be seen that B is the foot of the perpendicular from A to the x-axis, so OB=a, AB=b. Triangle AOB is a right triangle with OB and AB as the two right-angle sides, therefore its area is S_{\triangle AOB}=\frac12 ab. It is known that the area is 2, so \frac12 ab=2, obtaining ab=4. Also because A is on the inverse proportional function y=\frac{k}{x}, substituting A=(a,b) gives b=\frac{k}{a}, that is, k=ab. Therefore k=4.
